common_ground.text: The ZCG treasury has outgrown how ZCG works today. Critics and ZCG members agree it cannot handle this volume as it is.
Critical development work still needs funding. The argument is over who controls that money and who answers for it.

output.headline: Should ZCG end at NU8, with its 8% stream and treasury going to the NSM?
output.next: Draft ZIPs are filed by ebfull and thowar2, and joshs says his is coming. No vote or date is set. ebfull says ZCG promised its own plan and stayed silent through October.

stakes.decision: Whether the draft ZIPs ending the ZCG stream (ebfull's, thowar2's) go into a network upgrade. The thread sets no vote, poll or date.

unresolved.text: If ZCG's stream ends, who funds critical protocol work and the community projects that are not core?
How can the community's wish be measured, when a coinholder poll and a ZCAP poll would each be disputed?
What shows coinholder voting is more reliable than ZCG? Requests for evidence got no reply.

best_against.quote: Coinholders being diluted and that funding going somewhere the coinholders don't control, is already par for the course for 88% of the block subsidy.

best_for.quote: 72 ZCAP members (36%) have received ZCG grants. ZCAP members are behind about 75% of all the money ZCG has paid out. The people who pay have no say, the people who get paid do. This needs to change.

views.label: End ZCG and send its funds to the NSM
views.one_line: Holders pay for ZCG through dilution but do not control it, and it has funded things they voted against. Stop it and send its funds to the NSM; Coinholder grants continue.

best_against.quote: I don't see any signal that a dev fund is no longer needed. In fact we had important infrastructure, bug bounties and security initiatives funded fully by Coinholder Retroactive Grants.

best_for.quote: If dev funding is no longer needed, a better market signal is the retirement of the entire fund. A half measure leaves the door open to ongoing debate and politics.

views.label: Treat ZCG and Coinholder grants alike
views.one_line: Don't end only ZCG. End both funding streams, or neither. Some add that anonymous Coinholder votes need the same scrutiny as ZCG.

best_against.quote: There is no single organization on the planet that can efficiently and responsibly allocate such an enormous amount of capital when it was never designed or anticipated for that purpose.

best_for.quote: But all of this is not an argument against winding up the ZCG as an idea, but rather an argument against its current structure and incentives. In my opinion it is not sensible to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

views.label: Keep ZCG, but fix how it is run
views.one_line: ZCG has been careful and its failures are few. The problems are its structure, size and goals, so restructure it with experienced leadership and put the money to work.

best_against.quote: Not issuing to miners wasn't really the goal here; the payout and conditions of the NSM are subject to change anyway.

best_for.quote: is a decision to explicitly give more money to miners by decreasing the funding available for development and maintenance of the chain.

views.label: The NSM pays miners; development needs funding
views.one_line: Ending ZCG without a new development stream moves money from developers to miners, and the NSM only pays out from 2031. Dev funding should stay secured.

output.why_it_matters: ZCG gets 8% of each block reward and holds about $125M. The proposal sends that stream and the treasury to the NSM instead, so ZCG would approve no new grants.
